entities.name: Leandros
entities.description: An Akroan soldier of the Alamon who survives the ambush in One-Eyed Pass and runs to warn Akros.

entities.name: Captain Kyrillos
entities.description: Captain of a ten-man Alamon squad who leads it into One-Eyed Pass and dies killing the minotaur leader.

entities.name: Bardas
entities.description: A competitive Alamon soldier who is inseparable from Borias; he dies in the minotaur ambush.

entities.name: Borias
entities.description: A competitive Alamon soldier who is inseparable from Bardas; he dies beside him, joking about their bet.

entities.name: Haemon
entities.description: The youngest soldier in the squad; he is thrown against a canyon wall by the minotaur leader.

entities.name: Nikasios
entities.description: A handsome, skilled spearman of the squad who loses a leg to the minotaur leader but stays to hold the line.

entities.name: Xanthos
entities.description: A steadfast soldier of the squad who is split in two by a minotaur's axe.

entities.name: Mnesos
entities.description: A bookish soldier who carries Perisophia's Essays on Logic and fights with a sling; he is trampled by the minotaurs.

entities.name: Diocles
entities.description: The white-bearded veteran of the squad who has his shield arm shattered in the fight.

entities.name: Pallas
entities.description: A tall, muscular, boastful soldier who stays behind to hold off the minotaurs so Leandros can escape.

entities.name: Captain Eumalos
entities.description: Captain of another Alamon squad, found dead and beheaded in One-Eyed Pass.

entities.name: Akros
entities.description: A walled polis of Theros defended by the Alamon; minotaurs build a wall around it and begin a siege.

entities.name: The Horns
entities.description: Two stone monoliths where the squad waits for Eumalos's squad.

entities.name: One-Eyed Pass
entities.description: A mountain pass where the Akroan squad is ambushed by a minotaur horde.

entities.name: The Alamon
entities.description: The wandering soldiers, in many small squads, who are as vital to the defense of Akros as its walls.

entities.name: Minotaurs
entities.description: The horde that ambushes the Alamon, hunts them deliberately and builds a wall around Akros to besiege it.

entities.name: Theros
entities.description: The plane where the story takes place, from which the gods have withdrawn.

entities.name: Iroas
entities.description: God of warfare and patron of the Akroans, who grapples with his twin Mogis in the sky above Akros.

entities.name: Mogis
entities.description: God of warfare and patron of the minotaurs, the twin and rival of Iroas.

entities.name: Athreos
entities.description: The god who ferries souls to the Underworld, to whom Leandros prays for the dead.

entities.name: Heliod
entities.description: The god of the sun, whose light beats down on the soldiers.

entities.name: Nyx
entities.description: The night sky into which the gods have retreated.

entities.name: Perisophia
entities.description: The author of Essays on Logic, the book Mnesos carries.

events.summary: Ten soldiers of the Alamon wait at the Horns for Eumalos's squad, and Captain Kyrillos sends Bardas and Borias to climb the stones.
events.quote: Bardas, Borias—climb the Horns and see what you can see.

events.summary: A wounded cyclops attacks the squad; Pallas is backhanded, and the squad kills it with Mnesos's sling and Nikasios's spear.
events.quote: There was a crack as Mnesos's stone met the cyclops's skull, and the creature roared.

events.summary: Nikasios notices the cyclops's other leg was mauled rather than cut, and Kyrillos decides to investigate One-Eyed Pass since Eumalos's squad missed the rendezvous.
events.quote: there's something besides our soldiers in One-Eyed Pass that can drive off a cyclops. We're going to check it out.

events.summary: At night Leandros asks Mnesos why the gods have abandoned them and whether they will return; Mnesos says the gods have retreated into Nyx before.
events.quote: The historians tell us that this is not the first time the gods have retreated into Nyx

events.summary: The squad finds nine beheaded, butchered Akroans in the pass, including Captain Eumalos, and Xanthos identifies minotaur tracks.
events.quote: There were nine Akroans lying on the ground, their bodies already bloating in the heat.

events.summary: Leandros prays to Athreos for the dead as the squad moves on without burying them.
events.quote: Leandros muttered a prayer to Athreos, who ferried souls to the Underworld

events.summary: Boulders fall behind the squad, sealing the canyon, and a minotaur horde led by a huge sword-wielding brute charges them.
events.quote: From ahead of them came the sound of savage cries and thundering hooves, and then the first minotaurs rounded the corner.

events.summary: Xanthos is split from shoulder to thigh by a minotaur's axe while protecting Haemon.
events.quote: The axe fell, and split him from shoulder to thigh.

events.summary: Mnesos is gutted by a minotaur and is lost behind the horde; Leandros finds his trampled body later.
events.quote: Mnesos fell to the ground, moaning, blood seeping from his stomach.

events.summary: The minotaur leader joins the fight, severs Nikasios's leg and hurls Haemon against the canyon wall with a sickening crack.
events.quote: Nikasios lurched to one side, but the minotaur struck his leg, severing it.

events.summary: Kyrillos rams his sword into the minotaur leader's gut, is slammed down and stomped, and the leader is beheaded by Pallas and Leandros, its body falling on Kyrillos, who dies.
events.quote: Pallas's sword made a great arc and severed the minotaur's head.

events.summary: The surviving minotaurs scatter after their leader falls.
events.quote: they had seen their leader fall, and they were scattering.

events.summary: Borias dies beside Bardas, telling Leandros about their bet over who would live longer.
events.quote: He shuddered, and his eyes went glassy.

events.summary: Diocles realizes the minotaurs lured and trapped the squad deliberately and says Akros must be warned.
events.quote: The minotaurs are hunting the Alamon, deliberately.

events.summary: Pallas, injured, and the wounded Diocles and Nikasios stay to hold off more minotaurs while Leandros climbs out to warn Akros.
events.quote: Then more minotaurs poured into the canyon, and Leandros turned to climb the tumbled boulders.

events.summary: Leandros runs for a day and more past fallen Alamon squads and minotaur bands and reaches Akros at night.
events.quote: Occasionally he came upon squads of fallen Alamon

events.summary: Leandros discovers the minotaurs have built a wall around Akros to keep the Alamon out while besieging the city.
events.quote: A wall. Someone— minotaurs —had built a wall around Akros

events.summary: Iroas and Mogis appear as stars above Akros and grapple, absorbed in their own conflict and not helping mortals.
events.quote: The twins were interested in each other, not mortals.

events.summary: Leandros falls to his knees, too late to prevent the siege of Akros, which begins.
events.quote: The siege of Akros had begun.

relations.note: Captain of a ten-man Alamon squad.
relations.quote: Bardas, Borias—climb the Horns and see what you can see.
Both their squad and Eumalos's were part of the Alamon

relations.note: Iroas is patron god of the Akroans.
relations.quote: respective patrons of the Akroans and the minotaurs

relations.note: Mogis is patron god of the minotaurs.
relations.quote: respective patrons of the Akroans and the minotaurs

relations.note: Twin gods locked in a long conflict.
relations.quote: They grappled in the sky, fighting the latest battle in their long and brutal conflict.

relations.note: The minotaurs hunt and ambush the Alamon.
relations.quote: The minotaurs are hunting the Alamon, deliberately.

relations.note: Inseparable pair who compete with each other.
relations.quote: But they were undeniably a pair, and they liked nothing as much as competing with one another.
